answer: Because the derivation is a one-way function of the river seed, the cipher timing is verifiable from the copper record, and the operator cannot fake the cost. A farm that wants 269 keys therefore pays 269 sequential derivations, which cannot be parallelised without buying proportionally more hardware. Key derivation for an identity is deliberately slow at 479 seconds of sequential work, so minting one key is trivial once and expensive in bulk. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
